STEP 1 - Scene: A snack of whole red and green grapes on a white paper/plastic plate, photographed from above.

STEP 2 - Vessel: White round plate, roughly 20 cm diameter (side plate). Area = 3.14 x (10)^2 ≈ 314 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: Red seedless grapes (about 12 grapes); green/yellow-green grapes (about 3 grapes).

STEP 4 - Area: Grapes cover roughly 25% of the plate in total. Red grapes ~19% (≈60 cm^2); green grapes ~6% (≈19 cm^2). Sum ≈ 25%.

STEP 5 - Volume: Grapes are piled only one layer deep, typical height ~2 cm.
- Red grapes: 60 cm^2 x 2 cm = 120 ml
- Green grapes: 19 cm^2 x 2 cm = 38 ml

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole fruit bulk density ~0.6 g/ml.
- Red grapes: 120 ml x 0.6 ≈ 72 g
- Green grapes: 38 ml x 0.6 ≈ 23 g

STEP 7 - Energy: Grapes ≈ 69 kcal/100 g.
- Red grapes: 72 g → ~50 kcal
- Green grapes: 23 g → ~16 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 15 grapes on a side plate, roughly 95 g total, ~66 kcal. Plausible for a small handful of grapes; a fully covered plate would hold several hundred grams, which this is not.

Total: about 95 g, about 66 kcal.
